title: Tight junctions, desmosomes, gap junctions and plasmodesmata
caption: A tight junction seals the gap between animal cells so that nothing leaks between them; a desmosome joins two cells through cadherins anchored to intermediate filaments, so that pulling forces are spread through the tissue; a gap junction is a channel of connexins that joins the cytoplasm of the two cells. In plants, plasmodesmata are channels through the cell walls lined with plasma membrane. Drawn schematically: the sizes are not to scale.
alt: Four panels, each with two neighbouring cells. Tight junction: the membranes meet at the top and a dashed arrow trying to pass between the cells is blocked. Desmosome: dense plates inside each cell joined across the gap by cadherin lines, with filaments running into each cell. Gap junction: a channel through both membranes joining the cytoplasm of the two cells. Plasmodesma: two plant cells with walls and a middle lamella joined by a membrane-lined channel.
description: Tight junctions seal the gap, so substances must pass through the cells (gut lining, blood–brain barrier).
Desmosomes and adherens junctions link cells through cadherins attached to the cytoskeleton, spreading mechanical stress.
Gap junctions are channels of connexin that join the cytoplasm of neighbouring cells and let ions and small molecules (up to about 1 kDa) pass.
Plasmodesmata are channels through plant cell walls, lined with plasma membrane.
Schematic: the sizes are not to scale.

claims.text: at a tight junction the gap between the cells is closed
the cadherins are long enough to reach across the gap
each desmosome plaque is anchored to intermediate filaments in both cells
the gap junction channel reaches across the gap and is open
the plasmodesma channel is long enough to cross both walls and the middle lamella
